statement: Known invertible Mirror/basis transforms do not by themselves create fundamental rate-distortion gain when distortion is transformed consistently.
notes: Compression gains must come from noninvertibility, sharing, restricted codecs, or other real structure.

statement: Actual serializer accounting can change the hard-budget optimum relative to logical-bit accounting.
notes: A raw 76-bit state serialized to 88 bits and falsely passed an 80-bit raw check.

statement: Ignoring cross-block task coupling can underestimate distortion and produce false hard-budget passes.
notes: The tested naive diagonal model produced a false 32-bit pass.

statement: Quotienting safely equivalent optimizer states can substantially reduce exact search state.
scope: 16-leaf binary-mask toy; general rule requires equivalent future prerequisites/capabilities
notes: The archived toy had 2,090,918 recursive states vs 65,536 decoded masks (~31.9x). Canonical code uses decoded signature plus prerequisite signature; decoded mask alone is not a general safe key.

statement: Tree topology and precision can be complementary, so coordinate-wise optimization can miss a beneficial joint move.
notes: Joint move improved distortion by 6.40% at the same serialized budget; tree-only and precision-only gains were zero from the incumbent.

statement: In the D116 synthetic environment, a shared E coefficient across actions is decision-null for pairwise action differences.
notes: Absolute predictions need not be identical; pairwise decisions were identical in the tested construction.

statement: Very small coefficient spectral energy does not imply negligible decision value.
notes: Smallest tested mode carried ~0.019% Frobenius energy but hard removal was strongly harmful.

statement: Automatic spectral shrink rules D118-D120 improved the tested base but did not beat the best tested fixed q=0.75 rule.
notes: q=0.75 is empirical, not globally optimal or pathwise safe.

statement: For a 16-bit scalar baseline with N unique paid scalar values, a hard 64x payload target is B_total <= floor(N/4) bits.
notes: All paid decoder state must be included.

statement: A real compression claim requires exact paid-bit serialization plus a task-quality witness under a declared real-model extraction/evaluation contract.
notes: D56/D57 are the historical contract basis to reconstruct canonically.

statement: Search, query, calibration, validation, or controller work savings are not codec-bit savings unless the serialized decoder representation changes.
notes: Keep scheduler evidence in a separate lane.

statement: 64x compression on a real Transformer has not yet been demonstrated by the reconstructed evidence base.
notes: This is a status claim, not a theorem of impossibility.

statement: A QK near-tie boundary condition alone does not imply a low-dimensional routing tangent space in the Gaussian-null analysis used by the 2026-08-27 re-audit.
notes: Observed low-rank routing geometry in a real model would indicate additional structure such as shared Q/D subspaces, GQA/MQA, semantic clustering, or predictor/core reduction.

statement: When codec options conditionally require shared paid atoms, exact candidate rate is private payload plus the cost of the union of prerequisite closures; standalone per-block bit costs are generally nonseparable.
notes: A shared root/dictionary/basis is charged once regardless of consumer count. This is the allocation regime where FQC sharing can amortize fixed representation cost.
